notes: §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR1: "The beginning of a division in a program is indicated by the appropriate division header", and its end by the next division's header, the end program header, or "That physical position after which no more source program lines occur." The grammar states it structurally: programUnit is identificationDivision environmentDivision? dataDivision? procedureDivision? nestedProgram* endProgramHeader?, and environmentDivision, dataDivision and procedureDivision each open on their own header tokens, so a division's content is reachable only behind its header and closes at the next header, END PROGRAM or EOF. The one header the superset grammar leaves optional, IDENTIFICATION DIVISION (identificationDivision, the 2002 form), is required at --std 85 by VersionConformancePass.VisitIdentificationDivision (Constructs.IdentificationHeaderOptional2002, COBOL0900). Probed at 85: a unit opening on PROGRAM-ID is refused (COBOL0900); WORKING-STORAGE SECTION or a paragraph with no DATA or PROCEDURE DIVISION header, a division after a later one and a repeated DATA DIVISION are refused (COBOL0001); a three-program sequence whose divisions end at a header, at END PROGRAM and at end of source compiles and runs. The witness runs four headers in order, the last division ended by the end of the source.

next.reason: CHANGED: §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR1 'The beginning of a division in a program is indicated by the appropriate division header', and its end by 'The division header of a succeeding division in that program', 'The end program header' or 'That physical position after which no more source program lines occur'. §2023:10.3 (prose with no catalog row, kb/Work PB479) adds a case to the beginning: it is indicated 'by its division header or, in the case of the identification division when its header is omitted, by one of the paragraph headers permitted in the identification division', and the end 'by the beginning of the next division, an end marker for the source unit, or the end of the compilation group'. The catalogued rules that state parts of it: the identification division's format makes the header optional, '[ IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. ]' (§2023:11.2.1, FMT-11.2.1), where 1985 prints 'IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.' unbracketed (§1985:VI.3.2.1.1); and 'An end marker indicates the end of the specified source unit' (§2023:10.7.4 GR1), the end program header widened to every end marker. The words that differ: 'or, in the case of the identification division when its header is omitted, by one of the paragraph headers permitted in the identification division'. A program whose identification division begins at its PROGRAM-ID paragraph has no division beginning under the 1985 rule and is conforming 2023 source; a division that begins with its header ends at the same three places in both (a later division, the end marker, the end of the source).
